definitions.explanation: Doing something without particular intention or deliberate thought. Can describe actions done out of habit, idle curiosity, or without realizing their significance.

examples.english: I casually glanced out the window.

examples.japanese: {何気|なにげ}なく⟦{言|い}った→言う：00515_iu⟧⟦{一言|ひとこと}→一言：03708_hitokoto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{相手|あいて}→相手：01677_aite⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{傷|きず}つけた→傷つける：01935_kizutsukeru⟧。
examples.english: A casual remark I made hurt the other person.

examples.japanese: {何気|なにげ}なく⟦テレビ→テレビ：01536_terebi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つけたら→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧、⟦{好|す}き→好き：02355_suki⟧な⟦{番組|ばんぐみ}→番組：01705_bangumi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦やっていた→やる：02980_yaru⟧。
examples.english: I turned on the TV without thinking, and my favorite show was on.

notes:
Describes doing something without particular intention or awareness. Very common in narratives to describe how someone stumbled upon something or did something significant without realizing it.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {何気|なにげ}なく⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧: to glance casually
- {何気|なにげ}なく⟦{言|い}う→言う：00515_iu⟧: to say offhandedly
- {何気|なにげ}なく⟦{聞|き}く→聞く：00483_kiku⟧: to ask casually
- ⟦{何気|なにげ}ない→何気ない：10576_nanigenai⟧⟦{一言|ひとこと}→一言：03708_hitokoto⟧: an offhand remark

FORMS:
- ⟦{何気|なにげ}ない→何気ない：10576_nanigenai⟧: the adjective form (casual, unintentional)
- {何気|なにげ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧: colloquial/casual variant, sometimes used to mean "actually" or "surprisingly" — considered non-standard by some

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦さりげなく→さりげない：07575_sarigenai⟧: unobtrusively, in a subtle way — implies deliberate subtlety, while {何気|なにげ}なく implies lack of deliberation
- ⟦ふと→ふと：00048_futo⟧: suddenly, by chance — focuses on the spontaneous moment rather than the casual manner
